ModMetaData.description:
Discord Community: https://discord.gg/eVBebZ2N9s Version: v0.2.3 (Target: RimWorld 1.6)
Regions and Societies — Realistic Planets 2 edition Official Wiki and Documentation: https://github.com/Regions-and-societies/Core-MMF/wiki
This is the Realistic Planets 2 build of Regions and Societies. It is identical to the standard mod except that it runs on the map-mode framework bundled with Realistic Planets 2 instead of the standalone Map Mode Framework. Use this edition if you play with Realistic Planets 2; use the standard edition otherwise. Do not run both editions, or both frameworks, at once.
Regions and Societies overhauls the world map into living geography: dynamic geographic provinces with terrain-aware borders, four-tier faction territory ownership, geography-driven faction placement, regional demographics, a population-density heatmap, trade roads and procedural ruins. It is the continuation of Regions and Territories under a new identity.
Features: - Geographic Domain Mapping: splits the world into dynamic provinces with clear, terrain-aware boundaries. - Territorial Ownership: a four-tier ladder from exclusive hold to loose claim, shaded on the map, with coastlines and mountains reading as real borders. - Geography-Driven Faction Placement: nations settle as contiguous territory, one settlement per region, weighing established claim against resources, shying away from rivals' ground, and squaring their domains off rather than spidering. - Regional Demographics: every region carries a deterministic demographic profile - age structure, sex ratio, xenotypes, ideoligions, wealth, education and employment - derived from the factions pressing on it, their tech and beliefs, and the land itself. Nothing is stored in your save. - Demographic Map Overlays: seven world-map overlays, one per axis, plus faction territory and population density, running on Realistic Planets 2's bundled map-mode framework. - Region Panel Breakdown: the expanded region readout shows the full demographic profile alongside ownership and economics. - One-Click Overlay Toggles: region borders and the Territories / Dwellings map modes each get their own toggle icon in the world-view controls. - Hooks for Other Mods: a public API lets war and drafting mods skew a region's sex ratio (drafts, combat losses) with generational recovery, and lets expansion mods rank territory the way core does. - Procedural Trade Infrastructure: trade roads between settlements and historical ruins across the world map.
*** BEST ON A NEW COLONY - EXISTING SAVES ARE SUPPORTED IN COMPATIBILITY MODE *** A world generated with the mod installed gets everything, including placement rules. A world already in progress is adopted in Compatibility Mode: provinces are drawn and territory is owned and shown, but placement stays with vanilla or whichever mod owns it. The mode is decided once per save and shown under Strict territorial ownership in the mod settings. Removing the mod from an in-progress save is not supported and will log errors.
Requires: Realistic Planets 2, Harmony
--- Changelog (v0.2.3) - Worldgen resilience with missing DLC content --- - Fixed: black world when DLC content is unresolved. Classic (no-expansion) ideoligion role naming crashed world generation when the Ideology DLC was missing but other content added classic leader-role precepts - including for the player faction, which the 0.2.2 guard could not reach. Role naming is now guarded directly: a missing foundation gets a fallback title, and any naming failure degrades to the fallback instead of a dead world. - Graceful DLC degradation in faction generation: a faction needing Royalty title content that isn't resolved is skipped with a single log line and the world generates without it; repeated skips log one line each instead of a wall of stacks. - Marked incompatible with Layered Atmosphere and Orbit (LAO): it restructures the planet-layer stack that faction placement hooks into, breaking world generation. - Dev quality-of-life: the map-mode test helper now only runs on -quicktest launches, so playing with dev mode on no longer pulls you to the world map after starting a colony.
